judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 2, which created an education savings account program paying 85 percent of the estimated statewide average state and local funding per public school student into accounts parents may spend on private school tuition and other approved education expenses, with program spending capped at $1 billion for its first two-year budget period. It passed the Texas Senate 19-12 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to adopt H.J.R. 2, which proposed a constitutional amendment barring the legislature from imposing a state estate, inheritance, or death tax, and from newly taxing or raising taxes on gifts and inheritances beyond what was in effect on January 1, 2025. The Texas House adopted it 112-29, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against adopting H.J.R. 2, which proposed a constitutional amendment barring the legislature from imposing a state estate, inheritance, or death tax, and from newly taxing or raising taxes on gifts and inheritances beyond what was in effect on January 1, 2025. The Texas House adopted it 112-29, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to adopt H.J.R. 4, which proposed a constitutional amendment barring the legislature from taxing securities transactions or imposing an occupation tax on registered securities market operators, while leaving general business, sales, and use taxes in place. The Texas House adopted it 111-31, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against adopting H.J.R. 4, which proposed a constitutional amendment barring the legislature from taxing securities transactions or imposing an occupation tax on registered securities market operators, while leaving general business, sales, and use taxes in place. judgments.yea_description: Voted to adopt H.J.R. 34, which proposed a constitutional amendment letting the legislature exempt from property taxation the added value that border security infrastructure gives to land in counties bordering Mexico. The Texas Senate adopted it 23-8, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against adopting H.J.R. 34, which proposed a constitutional amendment letting the legislature exempt from property taxation the added value that border security infrastructure gives to land in counties bordering Mexico. The Texas Senate adopted it 23-8, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to adopt S.J.R. 18, which proposed a constitutional amendment permanently barring the legislature from taxing the realized or unrealized capital gains of individuals, families, estates, or trusts, while leaving property, sales, and use taxes in place. Texas levied no such tax at the time, so the amendment prevented a future one rather than ending an existing one. The Texas Senate adopted it 24-6, placing it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to adopt H.J.R. 98, an application asking the U.S. Congress to call a convention under Article V of the U.S. Constitution, limited to proposing amendments that impose fiscal restraints on the federal government, limit its power and jurisdiction, and set term limits for federal officials and members of Congress. The Texas House adopted it 86-57. It is a request to Congress and was not placed before Texas voters.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 8, which required the sheriff of every Texas county that operates a jail to seek an agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement authorizing local officers to help enforce federal immigration law, created a state grant program to cover the costs, and let the attorney general sue a sheriff who does not comply. It passed the Texas House 86-47 and was signed into law.

It passed the Texas House 86-47 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to approve the final version of S.B. 17, which barred governments, companies, and certain individuals connected to countries designated as security threats from buying Texas real property, exempted U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents, made a violation by a covered individual a state jail felony, and let the attorney general force a sale. The Texas House approved it 85-57 and it was signed into law.

The Texas House approved it 83-47 and it was signed into law.
